strengths: Novel paradigm for scientific dynamics adaptation: Shifting from test-time gradient fine-tuning or contextual modulation to direct conditional weight generation via latent diffusion is an original and ambitious perspective for scientific machine learning.

Well-motivated architectural design: The weight graph formulation aggregates layer/channel connections to respect architectural topology, reducing token complexity relative to naive weight flattening. Moreover, introducing a functional consistency loss (L_func) directly tackles the fundamental multi-modality and parameter-degeneracy problem inherent to neural network weight spaces.

Comprehensive empirical validation: The framework is benchmarked across four standard PDE systems (Cylinder Flow, Lambda-Omega, Kolmogorov Flow, Navier-Stokes) and a real-world ERA5 wind dataset, comparing against foundation models (Poseidon, DPOT, MPP), meta-learning baselines (CAMEL, GEPS, CoDA), and weight-diffusion models (D2NWG, CVAE).

Thorough supplementary ablations: The manuscript provides insightful analyses in the appendix, including permutation robustness, out-of-domain environmental parameter extrapolation, cross-equation generalization, and generator scaling vs. baseline scaling comparisons.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a pre-constructed model zoo: DynaDiff requires pre-training and curating an offline model zoo of expert models across diverse environments. While the authors demonstrate that domain-adaptive initialization reduces this burden, this offline prerequisite remains substantial and less flexible than pure data-driven foundation models when encountering environments outside the pre-trained distribution family.

Parameter asymmetry between generator and predictor: The generator requires approximately 380M parameters (VAE + DiT) to synthesize a lightweight target model of ~1M parameters. While the small model offers fast rollout at inference, running the 380M generator at test time to produce the weights partially offsets the lightweight advantage in constrained edge environments.

Heuristic nature of theoretical guarantees: The generalization analysis in Appendix G relies heavily on strong, unverified assumptions (such as functional Lipschitz continuity of the generator with respect to the prompt and the VAE decoder), making the bounds largely an application of the triangle inequality rather than a rigorous generalization guarantee derived from network properties.

Domain-specific assumptions in the prompter: The explicit feature extractor relies on domain-specific fluid-mechanics quantities (such as enstrophy and kinetic energy). For general dynamical systems where such physical invariants are ill-defined or unknown, the prompter branch would require manual redesign.

Marginal statistical gains on specific benchmarks: As shown in Table 5, the performance gains over competitive baselines on Lambda-Omega (p=0.53 out-domain) and Kolmogorov Flow in-domain (p=0.49) are not statistically significant.

strengths: Original and timely formulation: Transitioning cross-environment adaptation in scientific ML from gradient-based meta-learning or heavy foundation models to direct weight-space generative diffusion is conceptually innovative.

Principled technical designs: The framework thoughtfully addresses core failure modes of weight-space learning via (1) a weight-graph representation that preserves architectural connectivity, (2) a functional loss that aligns behavioral similarity rather than brittle parameter MSE, and (3) a hybrid physical-spectral prompter for conditioning on short observation snippets.

Extensive and rigorous empirical evaluation: The method is validated on four PDE systems (Cylinder Flow, Lambda-Omega, Kolmogorov Flow, Navier-Stokes) and the real-world ERA5 dataset. It consistently outperforms foundation models (DPOT, Poseidon, MPP), meta-learning approaches (DyAd, CAMEL, GEPS), and recent weight-generation baselines (D2NWG, CVAE).

Comprehensive analysis and ablations: The manuscript includes thorough investigations into weight permutations, extrapolation regimes, unseen governing equations, attention-map explainability, sampling stability, and runtime/memory profiling.
weaknesses: Asymmetry in model scale between generator and target predictor: The generator itself contains ~380M parameters (VAE + DiT) to synthesize a compact ~1M parameter FNO. While test-time inference on the generated FNO is very fast and lightweight, generating the weights still requires running a multi-step 380M diffusion model.

Scalability to larger predictor architectures: While the paper shows linear parameter scaling with target depth and width, scaling weight-space diffusion to full-scale 3D foundation neural operators (tens or hundreds of millions of parameters) remains non-trivial and unverified.

Reliance on model zoo curation: Training the diffusion framework requires building a zoo of well-converged expert models across seen environments. Although the proposed domain-adaptive initialization significantly mitigates the training cost per expert, this prerequisite still imposes an offline computational and storage overhead.

Theoretical bounds in Appendix G rely on strong assumptions: The generalization error analysis decomposes the error nicely but relies on assumptions such as functional Lipschitz continuity and bounded latent diffusion error without formal proofs of the constants under realistic network parameter distributions.

strengths: Novel and timely formulation: Transitions cross-environment dynamics adaptation from conventional gradient-based fine-tuning or low-dimensional context modulation to generative weight synthesis via latent diffusion.

Principled architectural and objective design: The weight graph representation effectively models the forward data-flow topology of neural operators; the node-attention VAE coupled with a functional consistency loss addresses parameter non-uniqueness and focuses on functional behavior rather than raw weight MSE.

Well-designed dynamics prompter: The hybrid prompter sensibly blends macroscopic physical invariants (moments, energy, enstrophy) with microscopic spectral temporal representations (FFT + GRU), capturing essential dynamical signatures from short observation trajectories.

Comprehensive and rigorous empirical evaluation: The paper demonstrates strong empirical performance across four canonical PDE benchmarks and real-world ERA5 data against both foundation models and meta-learning baselines, supplemented by extensive ablations (e.g., graph vs. sequence, one-stage vs. two-stage, permutation robustness, extrapolation, and statistical significance testing).
weaknesses: High upfront generator complexity and training overhead: Synthesizing a ~1M parameter predictive operator requires a ~380M parameter generative backbone (VAE + DiT) and pre-building an offline model zoo of expert models across environments. Although amortized and mitigated by domain initialization, this represents a substantial upfront compute requirement.

Architectural specificity: The generative pipeline is tied to generating fixed-topology expert architectures (e.g., specific FNO, UNO, or WNO dimensions), which limits flexibility when target systems require fundamentally different model capacities or operator topologies.

Heuristic nature of theoretical bounds: The generalization error analysis in Appendix G relies on strong functional Lipschitz assumptions (Assumption 1 and 3) that are postulated rather than rigorously derived from the dynamics or network parameterization.
